Turns your rooted Android phone into a hardware-level USB Video Class (UVC) webcam using ConfigFS (f_uvc) and V4L2, requiring zero host drivers on Linux, Windows, or macOS.
How do I use the app?

1. Grant root permissions (Magisk / KernelSU / APatch) and Camera permission.

2. Connect your phone via USB to your computer and tap "Start USB Webcam".

3. Open any webcam application on the host PC (OBS, ffplay, Cheese, Zoom, Browser) and select the USB webcam (supports MJPEG up to 1080p@60fps and YUYV up to 720p).
Does it work with the screen turned off?
Yes! Streaming runs inside a Camera Foreground Service with a partial wake lock, and the local viewfinder preview is disabled by default to save GPU and display power.
What formats are exposed over USB?
Format 1 is MJPEG (1920x1080, 1280x720, 640x360 at 60/30/15 fps).\nFormat 2 is Uncompressed YUYV (640x360, 640x480, 1280x720).

When functions/uvc.0 is linked into ConfigFS and bound to the UDC controller, the kernel creates a new V4L2 output node in /sys/class/video4linux/video* linked to the USB gadget. The app automatically detects it, applies SELinux policies (ioctl/map/read/write), and starts the native UVC responder loop.
How do I report bugs or submit feature requests?
See the Troubleshooting page to inspect Root status, /dev/videoX permissions, and CONFIG_USB_CONFIGFS_F_UVC kernel support.
The webcam doesn\'t enumerate on my PC, how do I fix it?
Try toggling \"Pure UVC-only mode\" or lowering \"UVC Isochronous Max Packet Size\" to 1024 in Settings if your USB hub or controller has limited isochronous bandwidth.

This app uses root (libsu) and Linux ConfigFS (CONFIG_USB_CONFIGFS_F_UVC) to expose your phone\'s Camera2 feed as a standard hardware USB webcam (/dev/videoX).\n\nWhen active, MTP/ACM are temporarily unlinked so the DWC3 USB controller has enough endpoints for UVC + ADB, and automatically restored when you tap Stop.
